text:
Maya: FYI - seeing a big latency regression in eu-west since 1710601100. p95 from ~120ms -> ~780ms, error rate up ~0.6%. GPU pool reports degraded nodes. Auto-failover moved ~30% traffic to us-west and that's now near capacity.
Pranav: copying. Is this the new runtime patch we deployed last night?
Maya: suspecting the KV-cache change in runtime v3.4.1 — we see cache miss amplification and huge batch queueing.
Oliver: SRE-Bot created INC-2026-0289 and alerted on-call. Link: https://incidents.redwood.local/INC-2026-0289 :rotating_light:
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-2026-0289 created: eu-west inference latency spike, suspected runtime KV cache regression. Severity: Sev2.
Jess: Any quick mitigation we can push to buy time? Disable batching? Route traffic?
Maya: disabling continuous batching reduced tail a bit in the canary, but cost per-token shot up. Still better than 800ms p95.
Pranav: Recommend: 1) Shift traffic off eu-west to reduce load, 2) Rollback runtime to v3.4.0 on serving fleet, 3) Spin up extra dedicated GPUs in us-west as temporary capacity.
Leo: On scaling — autoscaler isn't triggering fast enough because drain protection on some nodes is blocking scale up. I'll set aggressive scale policy for the next 30m.
OpsRun: Running route shift now: `redwoodctl routes update --region eu-west --traffic 0.05 --reason "failover-eu-west-latency"` -> shifting to 5% to test then to 0%.
Maya: After dropping batch to single-request mode and shifting to 5% traffic, p95 in eu-west dropped to ~320ms but queue length still high.
Oliver: Logs show a storm of KV cache evictions: `kv_cache.evictions/s = 4500` vs normal ~200. Also OOMs on a few infer nodes.
Pranav: Rolling back runtime on a small subset first. Command:```\n# rollback rollout\nredwoodctl rollout set --service inference-runtime --version v3.4.0 --selector region=eu-west --concurrency 4\n```
Jess: Prod rollback started on 4 nodes. Monitoring.
SRE-Bot: Alert: us-west GPU pool utilization 94% after traffic shift. New queue depth +40%.
Leo: I'm forcing additional dedicated capacity in us-west: `cloud provider spin-gpu --zone us-west-2 --count 8 --type a100` and bumping pool config. This will cost more short-term but avoids customer-visible errors.
Maya: After rollback to v3.4.0 on eu-west nodes we saw p95 back to ~130ms on those nodes. Good signal that KV change introduced regression.
Pranav: Next steps: 1) Halt further rollout of v3.4.1, 2) Create hotfix to KV cache eviction logic, 3) Run longer canary with load profile, 4) Rebalance traffic gradually.
Jess: I've updated runbook and pinged support/customer-success. Notifying affected customers via status page.
OpsRun: Reverting route to send 100% back to eu-west gradually: `redwoodctl routes update --region eu-west --traffic 0.75` -> will observe for 2 minutes.
Maya: Note on costs — temporary dedicated GPU spin-up will add ~+$7k/day; we'll include in postmortem.
Oliver: Putting a temporary autoscaler override on eu-west to be conservative (min nodes up) so we don't thrash during warmup.
Leo: Follow-up: create a short-lived mitigations doc in docs/incident/INC-2026-0289.md and tag eng-runtime + eng-sre.
Pranav: Postmortem owners: Maya (runtime), Leo (infra), Jess (customer comms). I'll draft timeline and include metrics (p95, evictions, queue depth, GPU utilization).
Maya: Thanks team. Closing loop: rollback + disable batching + short-term capacity increase fixed customer impact. Will keep monitoring next 4 hours and then start RCA on KV cache algorithm. :white_check_mark:
Jess: Thx — will update the incident ticket and status page.
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-2026-0289 status -> mitigated at 1710601540.
